message.content: {"caption":"Stacked area chart of cumulative estimated costs across a normalized timeline, divided among environment scaling, RSI infrastructure and GPU, and agent judging, verification, and attribution.","description":"The horizontal axis is “Normalized timeline (%)”, running from 0 to 100 with ticks at 0, 25, 50, 75, and 100. The vertical axis is “Cumulative cost (k USD)”, with ticks from 0 to 250 in steps of 50. Three smooth, stacked filled areas are identified by the legend: pale green, “environment scaling”; bright green, “RSI infrastructure, GPU”; and tan, “agent judge, verifier, attribution.” The top edge of each area is cumulative: the pale-green boundary rises early and levels off at about 130 k USD around 60% of the timeline; the bright-green layer becomes substantial later and brings its cumulative top to about 200 k USD by 100%; the tan upper layer brings the total to about 242 k USD at 100%. The overall dark-green-edged total rises throughout. Green arrows identify dark dots at about 38% and 115 k USD (“training start”) and about 60% and 175 k USD (“env. scaling end”); dotted vertical guides descend from both dots to the x-axis. Values below are estimated from the plotted curves, not printed point labels. At x ticks 0, 25, 50, 75, and 100, respectively, the estimated cumulative top edges are: environment scaling 0, 67, 125, 130, 130 k USD; RSI infrastructure, GPU 0, 67, 137, 184, 200 k USD; and total including the tan layer 0, 78, 145, 216, 242 k USD. The tan layer’s cumulative top edge is the total.
